words: IN THIS TOWN YOUR SHADOW CAN NEVER TOUCH
ANOTHER PERSON'S SHADOW
PEOPLE WALK SINGLE FILE ONE ARM APART
THE SIDEWALKS HAVE LANES PAINTED ON THEM
THE BUS HAS ONE SEAT PER
THE WEDDING PHOTO IN THE BAKERY WINDOW SHOWS A BRIDE AND GROOM SIX FEET APART HOLDING OPPOSITE ENDS OF A LONG WHITE RIBBON
AT NOON WHEN SHADOWS ARE TINY THE WHOLE TOWN COMES OUT TO SHOP
THE SECOND THE SUN GETS LOW EVERYONE SPRINTS INDOORS
WE MOVED HERE IN THE SPRING NOBODY TOLD US THE RULE
MY FIRST MORNING I WALKED TO SCHOOL NEXT TO A KID NAMED THEO SHOULDER TO SHOULDER
AND OUR SHADOWS CROSSED ON THE SIDEWALK
THE WHOLE STREET ROSE
A WOMAN DROPPED HER GROCERIES
THE CROSSING GUARD BLEW HIS WHISTLE UNTIL HE RAN OUT OF AIR
THEO'S MOM YANKED HIM INTO A HEDGE
A MAN ON A LADDER CLIMBED HIGHER INSTEAD OF COMING DOWN
ALL DAY EVERYWHERE I WENT PEOPLE SHUFFLED SIDEWAYS AWAY FROM ME
LIKE I WAS DRAGGING SOMETHING BEHIND ME
NOBODY WOULD SAY WHY
THAT EVENING THE SUN WENT ORANGE
AND EVERY SHADOW IN TOWN STRETCHED
ACROSS THE STREET LIKE LONG BLACK FINGERS
MAN RAN FOR HIS PORCH HIS SHADOW SLID OVER HIS NEIGHBOR'S SHADOW ON THE FENCE
JUST FOR A SECOND
BOTH SHADOWS TURNED THICK AND BLACK LIKE TAR AND THEN OUT OF THE DARK SEAM WHERE THEY OVERLAPPED SOMETHING CLIMBED UP
TALL THIN FLAT AS
PAPER NO FACE NO FRONT NO BACK JUST DARK
IT'S STOOD BETWEEN THE TWO MEN AND TURNED ITS HEAD FROM ONE TO THE OTHER LIKE IT WAS CHOOSING
THEN IT FOLDED ITSELF AROUND THE MAN FROM THE PORCH AND BOTH OF THEM SLID DOWN INTO THE PAVEMENT JUST HIS SHOES LEFT ON THE STEP
THE NEXT MORNING I GRABBED MY BIKE AND RODE FOR THE TOWN LINE
I COULD SEE THE SIGN
I COULD SEE THE HIGHWAY
THEN PEOPLE STARTED STEPPING OUT OF THEIR HOUSES
DOZENS THEN HUNDREDS
THEY SPREAD ACROSS THE WHOLE ROAD IN A PERFECT CHECKERBOARD NOBODY'S SHADOW TOUCHING ANYBODY'S
ISLAND THE MAYOR STEPPED FORWARD
EVEN HIS SHADOW WORE A LITTLE HAT
YOU CROSSED A SHADOW HE SAID
TONIGHT IT COMES FOR YOU OR FOR THE
BOY IT ONLY EVER TAKES ONE HE POINTED BACK TOWARD THE SQUARE SO WE DECIDE WHICH ONE
THEY SAT ME DOWN IN THE MIDDLE OF THE SQUARE AT SUNSET THEN THE WHOLE TOWN BACKED INTO THE DOORWAYS AND UNDER THE AWNINGS
INTO THE SHADE WHERE NOBODY CASTS A SHADOW AT ALL I WAS THE ONLY SHADOW IN THE SQUARE
IT STRETCHED OUT IN FRONT OF ME LONGER AND LONGER
ALL THE WAY TO THE FOUNTAIN
DON'T MOVE THE MAYOR CALLED FROM THE SHADE
THE STREET LIGHTS DIED ONE BY ONE AND THE THING CLIMBED UP OUT OF MY OWN SHADOW
RIGHT BETWEEN MY FEET IT ROSE UP TALLER THAN THE TOWN HALL FLAT AND BLACK AND BENT DOWN UNTIL THE
PLACE WHERE ITS FACE SHOULD BE WAS AN INCH FROM MINE IT STUDIED
ME THEN IT REACHED ONE LONG ARM DOWN AND IT TOUCHED MY SHADOW AND NOTHING HAPPENED IT TOUCHED
IT AGAIN NOTHING IT TILTED ITS HEAD LIKE IT DIDN'T UNDERSTAND
THEN FOOTSTEPS
THEO RAN OUT OF THE SHADE AND INTO THE SQUARE STRAIGHT AT ME YELLING MY NAME
HIS SHADOW SLAMMED INTO MINE AND THE TWO SHADOWS PILED
ON TOP OF EACH OTHER INTO ONE THICK BLACK POOL AROUND OUR FEET AND THE THING FLINCHED IT PULLED ITS ARM BACK LIKE THE GROUND WAS HOT
IT COULDN'T STEP ON A SHADOW THAT THICK WHERE OUR SHADOWS OVERLAP THERE WAS NO SEAM TO CLIMB OUT OF
IT WASN'T THE TOUCHING
IT WAS NEVER THE TOUCHING
IT ONLY EVER CAME FOR THE PEOPLE STANDING ALONE
FOR FIFTY YEARS THIS TOWN
HAD BEEN SPACING ITSELF OUT LIKE A BUFFET
HANDING IT ONE LONELY PERSON AT A TIME
I GRABBED THEO'S HAND AND YELLED AT THE DOORWAYS AND TOGETHER NOBODY
MOVED THEN AN OLD WOMAN STEPPED OUT OF THE BAKERY AND PUT
HER SHADOW ON OURS THEN THE CROSSING GUARD THEN THEO'S MOM THEN ALL OF THEM HUNDREDS
POURING OUT OF THE SHADE PILING THEIR SHADOWS INTO ONE GIANT BLACK PUDDLE ACROSS THE WHOLE SQUARE
THE THING GOT THINNER AND THINNER SMALLER AND
SMALLER UNTIL IT WAS A SINGLE BLACK THREAD WHIPPING AROUND ON THE COBBLESTONES
LOOKING FOR A CRACK TO SLIDE INTO AND THEN IT
FOUND ONE THE MAYOR HE WAS STILL STANDING AT THE VERY BACK OF THE SQUARE
ALONE UNDER THE ONE STREET LIGHT THAT STILL WORKED
WITH HIS OWN LITTLE SHADOW AND HIS
OWN LITTLE HAT
NOBODY HAD EVER BEEN ALLOWED CLOSE ENOUGH TO TOUCH IT THE THREAD SLID UNDER HIS SHOE THE STREET LIGHT DIED
NOW THE MAYOR'S SHADOW WAVES AT ME WHEN HE ISN'T LOOKING
LIKE AND SUBSCRIBE OR STAND CLOSER TO SOMEBODY
